stem: A 55-year-old patient has anemia, tingling in the feet, and increasing difficulty walking. Investigation identifies deficiency of a stomach-derived factor needed for intestinal absorption of an essential nutrient. Which of the following diagnoses best integrates the hematologic and neurologic findings with that absorption defect?

options.label: A
options.text: Bleeding from immune destruction of platelets
options.explanation: Immune platelet destruction explains low platelets and bleeding manifestations. It does not explain the identified vitamin absorption mechanism linking anemia with paresthesias and difficulty walking.
options.misconception: Explains the presentation through platelet loss while leaving the demonstrated nutrient-absorption defect unexplained.

options.label: B
options.text: Anemia from malaria activity within erythrocytes
options.explanation: Blood-stage malaria can produce anemia, but no parasite observation is supplied. More importantly, that explanation does not account for the demonstrated gastric-factor-dependent absorption defect.
options.misconception: Attributes anemia to erythrocytic infection without accounting for the measured gastric-factor-dependent absorption defect.

options.label: C
options.text: Anemia resulting from a lack of vitamin B12
options.explanation: B12 deficiency can produce anemia together with paresthesias and walking difficulty. Deficiency of gastric intrinsic factor links the intestinal absorption defect to this combined pattern.
options.misconception: No misconception: Impaired B12 absorption links the gastric-factor defect with the hematologic and neurologic findings.

options.label: D
options.text: Anemia from marrow stem-cell production failure
options.explanation: Aplastic marrow failure explains reduced blood-cell production, but it does not account for the specified intrinsic-factor-dependent vitamin absorption defect and accompanying B12-pattern neurologic findings.
options.misconception: Uses marrow production failure without explaining the specific absorption defect that unifies this pattern.

options.label: E
options.text: Anemia from excessive destruction of erythrocytes
options.explanation: Hemolytic anemia reflects destruction exceeding replacement. That mechanism does not integrate the stated gastric-factor deficiency and neurologic findings as directly as impaired B12 absorption.
options.misconception: Uses red-cell destruction to explain anemia while overlooking the nutrient-absorption and neurologic evidence.

context: Learning objective: integrate B12-related neurologic findings with anemia and impaired intrinsic-factor-dependent absorption. The mechanism connects a gastric absorption factor to intestinal vitamin uptake and subsequent blood-cell abnormalities.
